statement: Let S = sum_{i=0}^{m-1} rolls[i] and T = mean*(n+m) - S. The function returns a result r and the following two implications hold. (a) If n <= T <= 6*n, then len(r) = n, for every j with 0 <= j < n we have 1 <= r[j] <= 6, and S + sum_{j=0}^{n-1} r[j] = mean*(n+m). (b) If T < n or T > 6*n, then len(r) = 0.
preconditions: m = len(rolls); 1 <= m <= 100000; 1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= mean <= 6; for every i with 0 <= i < m, 1 <= rolls[i] <= 6.

statement: Let r1 and r2 be the results returned by the function on rolls1 and on rolls2 with the same mean and n. Whenever both calls return results, len(r1) = len(r2). If this common length is positive, then len(r1) = n and sum_{j=0}^{n-1} r1[j] = sum_{j=0}^{n-1} r2[j] = mean*(n+m) - sum_{i=0}^{m-1} rolls1[i]; if the common length is 0, then both calls return empty vectors.
preconditions: Let m = len(rolls1) = len(rolls2); 1 <= m <= 100000; 1 <= n <= 100000; 1 <= mean <= 6; for every i with 0 <= i < m, 1 <= rolls1[i] <= 6 and 1 <= rolls2[i] <= 6; and sum_{i=0}^{m-1} rolls1[i] = sum_{i=0}^{m-1} rolls2[i].
